_about: Hand-built care knowledge base for Florant. Checkpoint version: 10 species. Facts are summarised from general houseplant guidance (University of Missouri Extension houseplant guides, RHS growing guides). Member 1 verifies every entry against the source pages and adds exact URLs before the code freeze; target is about 30 species.

species.light: Bright, indirect light. Tolerates medium light but grows slowly and makes fewer leaf splits. Avoid strong afternoon sun, which scorches leaves.
species.watering: Water thoroughly when the top 3-5 cm of soil is dry, then let excess drain. Water less in winter.
species.humidity_temperature: Average to high humidity. Best at 18-27 °C; keep above 13 °C and away from cold draughts.
species.soil_feeding: Free-draining, chunky potting mix. Feed monthly in spring and summer.
species.common_problems: Yellow lower leaves usually mean overwatering; brown crispy edges suggest dry air or underwatering; no leaf splits suggest too little light.
species.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed (calcium oxalate).
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Monstera growing guide

species.light: Low to bright indirect light. Variegated forms keep their pattern better in brighter light.
species.watering: Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil is dry. Tolerates occasional drying out better than constant wet soil.
species.humidity_temperature: Average room humidity is fine. Best at 15-29 °C.
species.soil_feeding: Any well-drained potting mix. Feed every 4-6 weeks in the growing season.
species.common_problems: Yellow leaves often mean overwatering; limp, wilting leaves mean the plant is very dry; long bare stems mean too little light.
species.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed (calcium oxalate).
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Epipremnum growing guide

species.light: Very adaptable: from low light to bright light, including some direct sun.
species.watering: Let the soil dry out completely between waterings. In winter water only every 1-2 months.
species.humidity_temperature: Dry air is fine. Keep above 10 °C.
species.soil_feeding: Cactus or gritty, fast-draining mix. Feed lightly 2-3 times in summer.
species.common_problems: Soft, mushy, yellow leaves at the base mean root rot from overwatering — the most common cause of death.
species.toxicity: Mildly toxic to cats and dogs if eaten.
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Sansevieria growing guide

species.light: Low to bright indirect light. Avoid harsh direct sun.
species.watering: Stores water in thick rhizomes: let the soil dry out completely before watering, roughly every 2-3 weeks.
species.soil_feeding: Well-drained potting mix. Feed a few times in spring and summer.
species.common_problems: Yellowing leaves and soft stems usually mean overwatering.
species.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if eaten.
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Zamioculcas growing guide

species.light: Low to medium indirect light. Direct sun burns the leaves. More light gives more flowers.
species.watering: Keep the soil lightly moist but not soggy. The plant droops visibly when thirsty and recovers quickly after watering.
species.humidity_temperature: Likes higher humidity. Best at 18-27 °C, away from cold draughts.
species.soil_feeding: Moisture-retentive but well-drained mix. Feed monthly in spring and summer.
species.common_problems: Brown leaf tips come from dry air, irregular watering or salts in tap water; no flowers means too little light.
species.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed (calcium oxalate).
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Spathiphyllum growing guide

species.light: Bright, indirect light. Tolerates medium light.
species.watering: Keep the soil evenly moist in spring and summer; let the top few cm dry in winter.
species.soil_feeding: General potting mix. Feed monthly in the growing season.
species.common_problems: Brown leaf tips are common and are linked to dry soil, low humidity or fluoride and salts in tap water.
species.toxicity: Generally considered non-toxic to cats and dogs.
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Chlorophytum growing guide

species.light: Bright light with some gentle direct sun. Rotate the pot so it grows evenly.
species.watering: Water when the top 3-5 cm of soil is dry; water less in winter.
species.humidity_temperature: Average to high humidity. Best at 16-24 °C. Dislikes draughts and being moved.
species.soil_feeding: Well-drained potting mix. Feed monthly in spring and summer.
species.common_problems: Dropping leaves after a move or draught is common; brown spots in the middle of leaves often mean overwatering.
species.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if eaten (irritating sap).
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Ficus growing guide

species.light: Bright light with several hours of direct sun, for example a sunny window.
species.watering: Water deeply, then let the soil dry out completely. Water very little in winter.
species.humidity_temperature: Dry air is fine. Keep above 10 °C.
species.soil_feeding: Cactus and succulent mix in a pot with drainage holes. Feed lightly in summer.
species.common_problems: Soft, brown or mushy leaves mean overwatering; thin, pale, stretched growth means too little light.
species.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if eaten.
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Aloe growing guide

species.light: Bright, indirect light; tolerates some direct morning sun.
species.watering: Water when the top 3-5 cm of soil is dry. Reduce watering in winter.
species.soil_feeding: Well-drained potting mix. Feed monthly in spring and summer. Wipe dust off the leaves.
species.common_problems: Yellow, dropping lower leaves usually mean overwatering; leggy growth means too little light.
species.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if eaten (irritating sap).
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Ficus growing guide

species.light: Medium to bright indirect light. Tolerates lower light.
species.watering: Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil is dry.
species.humidity_temperature: Average to high humidity. Best at 18-27 °C.
species.soil_feeding: Well-drained potting mix. Feed monthly in spring and summer.
species.common_problems: Yellow leaves often mean overwatering; small leaves with long gaps between them mean too little light.
species.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed (calcium oxalate).
sources: University of Missouri Extension — houseplant care guides
RHS — Philodendron growing guide
